assessment.summary: One cross-cutting authorization-control opportunity: resolve a full principal at the auth boundary and enforce tenant scope and grant authority through a single owned service.

assumptions: No measured latency or memory budget was supplied.

opportunities.title: Centralize principal authorization and tenant scoping
opportunities.summary: Resolve subject, organization, and role scope into one principal at authentication, and enforce tenant bounds and grantor authority through one authorization service.
opportunities.diagnosis: Route-level auth compares only permission strings; tenant scope and grantor authority are never checked, producing two independent authorization bypasses.

evidence.claim: hasPermission checks only resource:action tokens; ApiKeyContext carries no organizationId
roleIds and permissions from request bodies are persisted without grantor-authority checks
Org-scoped key created and updated a device in another organization via HTTP
Non-admin user manager created a *:* role, assigned it, and governance returned allow
RoleScope declares org/site boundaries that no enforcement point consumes

desiredInvariants: Every request resolves exactly one principal with subject, organization, and role scope.
Every repository read or mutation is bounded by the principal's scope.
No grantor may create or assign authority beyond their own.

options.title: Strengthen local route guards
options.summary: Patch each affected route with org predicates and grantor-subset checks.

findingCoverage.rationale: Org predicates are the direct fix for each route.
Grantor-subset checks are the direct fix for each grant route.

tradeoffs.assessment: Known paths are closed; recurrence risk remains because the control is duplicated per route.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Re-run both PoCs and audit every route for org predicates.
No benchmark needed beyond existing request tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: Bad grants fail before persistence; guard drift remains a reliability risk.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Regression suite for each route group.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new operational burden; little central observability for denials.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm route errors are observable in logs.

tradeoffs.assessment: Small per-route changes; no data migration.

residualRisks: Inconsistent tenant predicate semantics between handlers

workPackages: Add org predicates and grantor checks per route; add regression tests.
acceptanceCriteria: Both PoCs return 403 for the crossing/grant actions.

options.title: Central resolved principal and authorization service
options.summary: Resolve subject, organization, and role scope at authentication; enforce tenant bounds and grant authority through one authorization service used by all routes.

findingCoverage.rationale: Tenant predicate becomes a property of the shared authorization boundary.
Grantor authority is compared inside the shared service.

tradeoffs.assessment: Both findings closed at one control point; future routes inherit the boundary.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Re-run PoCs; add a route-audit lint rule banning direct findAll() in handlers.

tradeoffs.assessment: One user+roles lookup per request on the auth path; cacheable.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark requests/sec before/after with and without cache.

tradeoffs.assessment: Small principal context per request; no retained growth.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Observe RSS under load if desired.

tradeoffs.assessment: Central failure point, but small and exhaustively tested; denials become consistent.
Single place to log/alert denied cross-tenant and grant-denied events.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Add structured denial logging and verify in integration tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: Context type change, repository signature change, route refactor across ~20 handlers.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Migrate one route group at a time with green tests.

residualRisks: Single authorization service becomes a prime target; keep it minimal and tested
Org resolution depends on the subject's user record being present

acceptanceCriteria: No route calls repository findAll/findById without tenant scope
migrationNotes: Keep Option 1 guards until each group migrates
implementationReadiness.rollback: Reintroduce the old context type behind a flag while keeping tenant predicates.

options.title: Per-tenant service and store isolation
options.summary: Deploy one application/store unit per organization behind a tenant-routing edge.

findingCoverage.rationale: Cross-tenant repository access is structurally impossible, but route-level tenant binding is still needed at the edge.
Isolation limits blast radius to one tenant but does not stop intra-tenant role escalation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Strongest containment for tenant data; grant escalation still needs Option 1/2 checks.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Tenant-level integration tests across deployed units.

tradeoffs.assessment: Additional edge hop and per-tenant connections.

tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure per-tenant footprint at target tenant count.

tradeoffs.assessment: More moving parts; failure modes multiply.
Fleet provisioning, monitoring, and secret management multiply.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Trial deployment of two tenant units.

tradeoffs.assessment: Requires deployment architecture change; current single-node SQLite/file model does not support it directly.

workPackages: Move JWT/secret management to per-tenant scope
acceptanceCriteria: Tenant A cannot reach tenant B store at the network layer
migrationNotes: Requires Option 2 grant checks inside each tenant

opportunities.recommendation: Adopt the central principal/authorization-service design; use local guards only as an interim patch.

openQuestions: Should API keys be bound to an organization at provisioning time?
Should JWT claims carry the org or be resolved per request?
Do planned downstream services need explicit cross-tenant grants?
